atoms.sentence: A symptom (from Greek , "accident, misfortune, that which befalls", from , "I befall", from - "together, with" and , "I fall") is a departure from normal function or feeling which is noticed by a patient, reflecting the presence of an unusual state, or of a disease.

atoms.title: WikiHop support 03
atoms.sentence: A symptom is subjective, observed by the patient, and cannot be measured directly, whereas a sign is objectively observable by others.

atoms.title: WikiHop support 03
atoms.sentence: For example, paresthesia is a symptom (only the person experiencing it can directly observe their own tingling feeling), whereas erythema is a sign (anyone can confirm that the skin is redder than usual).

atoms.title: WikiHop support 03
atoms.sentence: Symptoms and signs are often nonspecific, but often combinations of them are at least suggestive of certain diagnoses, helping to narrow down what may be wrong.

atoms.title: WikiHop support 03

atoms.title: WikiHop support 04

atoms.title: WikiHop support 04

atoms.title: WikiHop support 04
